is_anopheles.evidence: The study assesses insecticide resistance in Anopheles gambiae s.l. and Anopheles funestus in Uganda (Abstract, Page 1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports frequencies for Vgsc L1014S (L995S) and L1014F (L995F) mutations (Abstract, Page 1; Table 2, Page 4).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 2 (Page 4) provides kdr allele frequencies with sample sizes (N) for multiple sites and time periods. Figure 3 (Page 5) provides genotype frequencies (RR, RS, SS) for bioassay survivors and dead mosquitoes.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from the field in seven districts across Uganda (Apac, Arua, Jinja, Kanungu, Kyenjojo, Mubende, and Tororo) between 2001 and 2006 (Materials and Methods, Page 1).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study reporting original collection, bioassay, and genotyping data.

sub_country_location.evidence: Data is reported for specific districts (e.g., Tororo, Apac) and villages (e.g., ADA, ADB, NAA, NAB) (Table 1, Page 3; Table 2, Page 4).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collection periods are clearly defined as 2001–2002 and 2004–2006, both within the 3-year window (Materials and Methods, Page 1; Table 2, Page 4).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The paper mentions that 2001-2002 samples were collected in the framework of a study described in Okello et al. 2006 (Ref 11), and the kdr assay was described in Verhaeghen et al. 2006 (Ref 10), but this appears to be the primary report for the full spatio-temporal kdr dataset.

supplement.evidence: All relevant genotype counts, frequencies, and bioassay results are contained within the main text, tables, and figures of the provided PDF.

assessment.summary: This study investigates the spatio-temporal distribution of kdr mutations (L1014S and L1014F) in Anopheles gambiae s.s. across seven districts in Uganda from 2001 to 2006. It reports a significant increase in L1014S frequency over time in several districts and correlates kdr genotypes with survival in WHO susceptibility bioassays for DDT and permethrin. It also examines the relationship between kdr frequency and Plasmodium falciparum infection status.
